Residents urged to report Hurricane Lowell home damage ahead of second FEMA assessment

LĪHUʻE – The County of Kauaʻi is urging residents whose homes sustained major damage from Hurricane Lowell, and who have not yet reported it, to do so now, ahead of a second federal damage assessment in December.

The County, in coordination with the Hawaiʻi Emergency Management Agency (HIEMA), will participate with the Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA) in a second Joint Preliminary Damage Assessment for Individual Assistance. A FEMA team is tentatively scheduled to arrive Dec. 7 and will have about two weeks to complete the assessment. HIEMA will confirm the final schedule.

The assessment follows FEMA's Oct. 21 denial of the state's request for Individual Assistance for Hurricane Lowell. Individual Assistance is the federal program that helps individuals and households. It is separate from the Public Assistance program, which has already been approved to help government agencies and eligible nonprofits recover.

Damage reports submitted now will help the County identify homes for FEMA teams to review so they can document the full scope of residential damage on Kauaʻi. Submitting a report does not guarantee federal assistance.

"This second assessment is a chance to make sure damaged homes aren't missed," said Kauaʻi Emergency Management Agency Administrator Elton Ushio. "Your report helps us guide FEMA teams to the homes they need to see. Please take a few minutes to submit yours."

Residents can submit damages through the Hurricane Lowell Residential Damage Report form through December 4, 2026. Residents without internet access may contact KEMA at 808-241-1800 or kema@kauai.gov for assistance.

Residents should have their home address, a description of the damage, and photos, if available, ready when they report. Residents who already reported damage in September do not need to submit again.

Residents should continue to file claims with their insurance companies for home damage and personal property losses.

Residents who need help with recovery resources may call 2-1-1 or visit www.kauairecovers.org .

For more information, please contact KEMA at 808-241-1800 or kema@kauai.gov.

To receive emergency alerts, sign up for Everbridge by visiting www.kauai.gov/KEMA and clicking "Notification Services," texting "KAUAIEMA" to 888777, or calling KEMA at 808-241-1800.

Inauguration of Kauaʻi County Council-elect, Mayor-elect scheduled Dec. 1

LĪHUʻE – The public is invited to attend the inauguration of the Kauaʻi County Council-elect and Mayor-elect Mel Rapozo on Tuesday, Dec. 1, 2026, at the Kauaʻi War Memorial Convention Hall (KWMCH). The ceremony begins at 1 p.m.

Before the ceremony, the Mayor-elect and Councilmembers-elect will be officially sworn in at noon. The Kauaʻi County Council will hold its inaugural meeting in the large meeting room at KWMCH. Councilmembers-elect are Paul Noboru Applegate, Addison Bulosan, Michelle Kaleiohi Correa, Fern Ānuenue Holland, Arryl Kaneshiro, Todd Ozaki, and Dane Smith.

Parking at KWMCH is limited. Motorists should expect possible traffic delays on Hardy Street and ʻUmi Street in Līhuʻe during the event. Please drive with caution and use alternate routes if possible.

For more information, please contact the Office of the County Clerk, Council Services Division at 808-241-4188 or cokcouncil@kauai.gov.

If you need an ASL interpreter, materials in an alternate format, or other auxiliary aid support, or an interpreter for a language other than English, please contact the Office of the County Clerk, Council Services Division at 808-241-4188 or cokcouncil@kauai.gov as soon as possible. Requests made as early as possible will allow adequate time to fulfill your request. Upon request, this notice is available in alternate formats such as large print, Braille, or electronic copy. *Officials advise no swimming, recreational ocean activities on north-facing shores*

HANALEI *– *Ocean Safety Bureau officials are advising no swimming or other recreational ocean activities along all north-facing shores of Kauaʻi today through Sunday, November 29, due to high surf and dangerous ocean conditions.

The National Weather Service has issued a High Surf Warning for north- and west-facing shores of Kauaʻi and Niʻihau, in effect through 6 a.m. Wednesday. The warning may be extended, dropped, or modified as conditions develop.

According to the NWS, a large, long-period north-northwest swell will build today, bringing surf to warning levels. A High Surf Warning remains in effect until 6 a.m. Wednesday for north- and west-facing shores of Niʻihau and Kauaʻi. Surf heights are forecast at 20 to 30 feet along north-facing shores and 15 to 20 feet along west-facing shores. Surf is expected to subside Wednesday, but an even larger north-northwest swell is likely Wednesday night into Thursday.

Forecasters say conditions will be hazardous, with very strong breaking waves and powerful currents. Waves breaking in channel entrances may make navigating the channels dangerous.

A Coastal Flood Statement is in effect from 6 p.m. this evening through Thursday morning for Niʻihau and Kauaʻi. Higher-than-predicted water levels, combined with the surf, could cause nuisance flooding of beaches that are normally dry, minor coastal erosion and saltwater inundation, particularly during the pre-dawn high tides Wednesday and Thursday mornings.

As a safety precaution, OSB officials have posted warning signs and are monitoring the area.

Entering the water in these areas in hazardous ocean conditions could cause serious injury or death. Beachgoers are also advised to use extreme caution, as large breaking waves could make it dangerous for those standing along the shoreline. When in doubt, don’t go out.

Beachgoers are urged to heed all posted warnings and advisories.

For updated information on ocean and weather alerts, visit the NWS website, www.weather.gov/hfo .

For up-to-date information about Kauaʻi ocean conditions and ocean safety, please speak to a county lifeguard at any lifeguard station, visit safebeachday.com/county/kauai , or call the Ocean Safety Bureau at (808) 241-4984. View as web page

*Christina Basuel recognized as KPDʻs November 2026
Employee of the Month*

 

LĪHU‘E – The Kauaʻi Police Department (KPD) announced Christina Basuel as the Employee of the Month for November at the Police Commission Meeting held on Friday, November 20, 2026. Ms. Basuel was recognized for her initiative, dedication, and excellent leadership in planning and executing KPDʻs inaugural Halloween Movie Night on October 23, 2026. The event brought in a crowd of 300 people and highlighted KPD’s ongoing commitment to the community.

“I am very pleased to have employees like Christina Basuel on my staff,” said Chief of Police Rudy Tai. “Her willingness to go above and beyond to create meaningful experiences reflects the values we stand for at KPD.”

In the aftermath of Hurricane Lowell when many families were struggling, Chief Tai wanted to host a cheerful, community Halloween event at the KPD headquarters. With just a few weeks to prepare, Ms. Basuel led a team to organize an event to remember. She showed resourcefulness and took on responsibilities well beyond her position as an Administrative Assistant I in the Criminal Investigations Division.

The event was a team effort among KPD employees, as well as various County of Kaua’i departments and organizations contributing and taking on extra duties. However, Ms. Basuel stood out by organizing the group, keeping everyone motivated, and overcoming challenges while staying focused on the goal.

Ms. Basuel demonstrated that leadership is not just about rank or title. She saw a chance to bring joy to the community during a difficult time, united people, and helped turn a big idea into reality. For her initiative, teamwork, perseverance, and dedication to building KPD’s positive relationship with the community, Christina Basuel is truly deserving of Employee of the Month.

Ms. Basuel also served as a police officer at KPD for five years, bringing her total service at KPD to 15 years.

Looking for a meaningful career where your work makes a real impact? KPD is actively recruiting dedicated individuals to join our team. The salary for a police officer ranges from approximately $83,000 to over $118,000 and includes a robust benefits package. Qualifications include a high school diploma or equivalent, a valid driver’s license, and a minimum age of 20 years. Applicants should not have any misdemeanor, felony or domestic violence convictions. To learn more about qualifications and how to apply, visit joinka View as web page

*Nov. 18, Hurricane Lowell recovery, County of Kauaʻi services update*

*LĪHUʻE* – Updates on Hurricane Lowell recovery and County of Kauaʻi services follow.

*_HURRICANE LOWELL RECOVERY_*

Recovery information is updated regularly at www.kauairecovers.org.

*Third Supplemental Emergency Proclamation*

Mayor Derek S.K. Kawakami signed a Third Supplemental Emergency Proclamation on Nov. 13. It extends the emergency period 60 days from signing, or until further action by the mayor, and continues the County’s disaster area designation.

The proclamation also ends the suspension of solid waste disposal fees at County landfills, refuse transfer stations, and debris recycling stations. Tipping fees resume Wednesday, Nov. 18.

*CASPER survey underway this week (NEW UPDATE)*

The Hawaiʻi Department of Health’s Kauaʻi District Health Office and the County are conducting the Hurricane Lowell CASPER survey through Friday, Nov. 20.

DOH teams, supported by the Kauaʻi Medical Reserve Corps and KEMA, are going door to door in 30 randomly selected areas, visiting seven homes in each. Team members wear identifying vests and carry ID cards.

The survey takes less than 10 minutes and is voluntary and confidential. No names or addresses are collected, and households may also respond by phone. Questions cover supplies right after the storm, physical and economic impacts, health and well-being, and recovery needs.

Results will be shared in a public report. Past reports are available at https://health.hawaii.gov/kauai/Casper.

*Agricultural recovery needs survey (NEW UPDATE)*

The Office of Economic Development (OED) is asking commercial farmers, ranchers, and agricultural businesses to complete a short survey on the ongoing impacts of Hurricane Lowell and the resources needed for recovery.


The survey asks about physical damage, lost revenue, disruptions to production and sales, current operating conditions, and outstanding recovery needs. Responses will help the County understand economic impacts across the agricultural sector and identify funding opportunities, programs, and other resources.

All commercial agricultural operations on Kauaʻi are encouraged to respond, including those that had no direct physical damage but were affected by lost sales, market disruptions, or other challenges. The survey takes about 10 minutes, and best estimates are fine if exact figures are unavailable. One response per business or operation is requested.

County announces holiday closures

LĪHUʻE – In observance of the Thanksgiving holiday, County of Kauaʻi offices and all neighborhood centers will be closed on Thursday, Nov. 26.

Closures also include the following facilities:

·     All refuse transfer stations;

·     The Kekaha Landfill;

·     All HI5 Redemption Centers;

·     The Līhuʻe Redemption Center;


·     The Puhi Metals Recycling Facility; and


·     The Kapaʻa swimming pool.

The schedule for residential refuse pick-up will remain unchanged.

The Kauaʻi Bus will be operating on its current daily schedule. 

Regular business hours for county offices and services will resume on Friday, Nov. 27.

For more information on recreation services, please visit the Department of Parks and Recreation website, www.kauai.gov/Parks , or call 808-241-4460.

For more information about The Kauaʻi Bus, please visit the Transportation website, www.kauai.gov/transportation , or call 808-246-8110.

GD-PIO NR 11-16-26 (Mayor Kawakami signs Bill 2998, bringing wildfire safety standards to new homes islandwide)
2026-11-17T00:21:29 [water, transit, county_services]
Mayor Kawakami signs Bill 2998, bringing wildfire safety standards to new homes islandwide

LĪHUʻE – On Monday, Nov. 16, Mayor Derek S.K. Kawakami signed into law Bill No. 2998, Draft 3, an ordinance passed by the Kauaʻi County Council on Oct. 28 that sets islandwide wildfire safety standards for new homes.

The ordinance establishes Wildfire and Wildland Urban Interface (WUI) construction requirements for new homes and substantial improvements, along with defensible space, setback, and access standards for larger new developments. It builds on Bill No. 2961, signed in September 2025, which made Kauaʻi the first county in Hawaiʻi to tie wildfire safety into zoning and permitting for West Kauaʻi’s plantation camp districts.

“Mahalo to the Kauaʻi County Council, our Planning Department, the Kauaʻi Fire Department, the Kauaʻi Emergency Management Agency, the Hawaiʻi Wildfire Management Organization, and the builders, designers, and residents who testified and helped shape this ordinance,” said Mayor Kawakami. “Lahaina taught all of Hawaiʻi that in a wind-driven fire, homes are lost to embers. We have a kuleana to learn from that before we face a disaster of our own. The homes we build today will be home to our keiki and kūpuna for generations, and this ordinance makes sure they are built with that lesson in mind.”

According to U.S. Department of Agriculture Forest Service data cited in the ordinance, homes in Kauaʻi County face a higher wildfire risk than about 91 percent of U.S. counties. The Lahaina Fire Incident Analysis Report also recommended WUI codes, ember-resistant construction, and defensible space requirements as key steps for wildfire safety statewide.

“As our climate changes, we have to do everything we can on the planning side before a fire ever starts,” said Council Planning Committee Chair Addison Bulosan. “No one takes added building costs lightly, and this Council spent months working through those questions with our community. In the end, protecting lives and homes is worth it.”

Under the ordinance, new homes will include home hardening standards, a non-combustible zone, and setback standards for future subdivisions.

“This ordinance was built for Kauaʻi, not copied from a mainland code,” said Planning Director Kaʻāina Hull. “Every requirement was weighed for its safety benefit, its cost, and whether it lets us keep building the housing our community needs. High Surf Warning in effect for Kaua‘i and Ni‘ihau Tuesday 6 a.m. through Wednesday 6 a.m.

The National Weather Service has issued a High Surf Warning for north- and west-facing shores of Kaua‘i and Ni‘ihau that will go into effect Tuesday, November 24, at 6 a.m. through 6 a.m. Wednesday, November 25. The warning may be extended, dropped, or modified as conditions develop.

According to the NWS, a large to extra-large, long-period north-northwest swell will produce high surf. Surf heights along north-facing shores are projected to reach heights of 20 to 30 feet. Surf heights along west-facing shores are projected to reach heights of 12 to 16 feet.

Entering the water in these areas during the High Surf Warning is very hazardous and could cause serious injury or death. Beachgoers are also advised to use extreme caution, as large breaking waves could make it dangerous for those standing along the shoreline.

For updated information on ocean and weather alerts, visit the NWS website, www.weather.gov/hfo .

For up-to-date information about Kaua‘i ocean conditions and ocean safety, please speak to a county lifeguard at any lifeguard station, visit https://safebeachday.com/county/kauai/ , or call the Ocean Safety Bureau at 808-241-4984.

items.subject: NR 11-20-26 (Christina Basuel recognized as KPDʻs November 2026 Employee of the Month)

headline.title: Christina Basuel recognized as KPDʻs November 2026 Employee of the Month
headline.subject: NR 11-20-26 (Christina Basuel recognized as KPDʻs November 2026 Employee of the Month)

items.body:
*Christina Basuel recognized as KPDʻs November 2026 
Employee of the Month*

 

LĪHU‘E – The Kauaʻi Police Department (KPD) announced Christina Basuel as the Employee of the Month for November at the Police Commission Meeting held on Friday, November 20, 2026. Ms. Basuel was recognized for her initiative, dedication, and excellent leadership in planning and executing KPDʻs inaugural Halloween Movie Night on October 23, 2026. The event brought in a crowd of 300 people and highlighted KPD’s ongoing commitment to the community.

“I am very pleased to have employees like Christina Basuel on my staff,” said Chief of Police Rudy Tai. “Her willingness to go above and beyond to create meaningful experiences reflects the values we stand for at KPD.”

In the aftermath of Hurricane Lowell when many families were struggling, Chief Tai wanted to host a cheerful, community Halloween event at the KPD headquarters. With just a few weeks to prepare, Ms. Basuel led a team to organize an event to remember. She showed resourcefulness and took on responsibilities well beyond her position as an Administrative Assistant I in the Criminal Investigations Division.

The event was a team effort among KPD employees, as well as various County of Kaua’i departments and organizations contributing and taking on extra duties. However, Ms. Basuel stood out by organizing the group, keeping everyone motivated, and overcoming challenges while staying focused on the goal.

Ms. Basuel demonstrated that leadership is not just about rank or title. She saw a chance to bring joy to the community during a difficult time, united people, and helped turn a big idea into reality. For her initiative, teamwork, perseverance, and dedication to building KPD’s positive relationship with the community, Christina Basuel is truly deserving of Employee of the Month.

Ms. Basuel also served as a police officer at KPD for five years, bringing her total service at KPD to 15 years.

Looking for a meaningful career where your work makes a real impact? KPD is actively recruiting dedicated individuals to join our team. The salary for a police officer ranges from approximately $83,000 to over $118,000 and includes a robust benefits package. Qualifications include a high school diploma or equivalent, a valid driver’s license, and a minimum age of 20 years. Applicants should not have any misdemeanor, felony or domestic violence convictions. To learn more about qualifications and how to apply, visit joinkauaipd.com .

headline.subject: NR 11-18-26 (Nov. 18, Hurricane Lowell recovery, County of Kauaʻi services update)

items.body:
*Nov. 18, Hurricane Lowell recovery, County of Kauaʻi services update*

*LĪHUʻE* – Updates on Hurricane Lowell recovery and County of Kauaʻi services follow.

*_HURRICANE LOWELL RECOVERY_*

Recovery information is updated regularly at www.kauairecovers.org.

*Third Supplemental Emergency Proclamation*

Mayor Derek S.K. Kawakami signed a Third Supplemental Emergency Proclamation on Nov. 13. It extends the emergency period 60 days from signing, or until further action by the mayor, and continues the County’s disaster area designation.

The proclamation also ends the suspension of solid waste disposal fees at County landfills, refuse transfer stations, and debris recycling stations. Tipping fees resume Wednesday, Nov. 18.

*CASPER survey underway this week (NEW UPDATE)*

The Hawaiʻi Department of Health’s Kauaʻi District Health Office and the County are conducting the Hurricane Lowell CASPER survey through Friday, Nov. 20.

DOH teams, supported by the Kauaʻi Medical Reserve Corps and KEMA, are going door to door in 30 randomly selected areas, visiting seven homes in each. Team members wear identifying vests and carry ID cards.

The survey takes less than 10 minutes and is voluntary and confidential. No names or addresses are collected, and households may also respond by phone. Questions cover supplies right after the storm, physical and economic impacts, health and well-being, and recovery needs.

Results will be shared in a public report. Past reports are available at https://health.hawaii.gov/kauai/Casper.

*Agricultural recovery needs survey (NEW UPDATE)*

The Office of Economic Development (OED) is asking commercial farmers, ranchers, and agricultural businesses to complete a short survey on the ongoing impacts of Hurricane Lowell and the resources needed for recovery.


The survey asks about physical damage, lost revenue, disruptions to production and sales, current operating conditions, and outstanding recovery needs. Responses will help the County understand economic impacts across the agricultural sector and identify funding opportunities, programs, and other resources.

All commercial agricultural operations on Kauaʻi are encouraged to respond, including those that had no direct physical damage but were affected by lost sales, market disruptions, or other challenges. The survey takes about 10 minutes, and best estimates are fine if exact figures are unavailable. One response per business or operation is requested.

The deadline is Monday, Dec. 7. Take the survey at https://survey123.arcgis.com/share/290e15370ab041b4b9552eccab196042.

The survey is for information-gathering and recovery planning only. It is not an application for financial assistance, and participation does not guarantee eligibility for future assistance. Agricultural organizations, industry partners, and community groups are encouraged to share the survey through their producer networks.

For questions, contact Niki Kunioka-Volz with OED at nkvolz@kauai.gov or 808-241-4951.

*Relief grants for farmers and ranchers*

Farms, orchards, ranches, and similar operations statewide affected by Hurricane Lowell or other recent storms may apply for up to $1,500 through the state Emergency Farmer Relief grant program. One check is issued per applicant per year. Applicants will need tax documents such as a W-9, Schedule C, or Schedule F.

Funding is limited, and overflow applications will be processed first-come, first-served. Checks are expected to be available for pickup statewide in early to mid-January 2027, and applicants will be notified of the time and place. Applications close Jan. 29, 2027.

Apply at https://dab.hawaii.gov. For questions, email dab.info@hawaii.gov or call 808-973-9560.

*Business Recovery Grants*

The Kauaʻi Hurricane Lowell Business Recovery Grant Program is no longer accepting applications due to high demand. Businesses and nonprofits can join the waitlist at https://kauaibusinessrecovery.o

paragraphs: The County is covering the $2.50 convenience fee for online vehicle registration renewals and sewer payments.

bullets: Waimea Neighborhood Center main hall (side rooms are open)

paragraphs: Morgan’s Pond at Lydgate Beach Park is closed until further notice due to logs and fine wood particles. Kekaha Neighborhood Center is accepting new online reservations at www.kauai.gov/parks. Kauaʻi Bus 900 and 950 express routes are not running.

paragraphs: Residents are encouraged to sign up for Everbridge emergency alerts. Visit www.kauai.gov/KEMA and click “Notification Services,” text “KAUAIEMA” to 888777, or call KEMA at 808-241-1800.
For updates on County services, working phone numbers, and visitor information, visit www.kauairecovers.org.

County announces holiday closures

LĪHUʻE – In observance of the Thanksgiving holiday, County of Kauaʻi offices and all neighborhood centers will be closed on Thursday, Nov. 26.

Closures also include the following facilities:

·     All refuse transfer stations;

·     The Kekaha Landfill;

·     All HI5 Redemption Centers;

·     The Līhuʻe Redemption Center;


·     The Puhi Metals Recycling Facility; and


·     The Kapaʻa swimming pool.

The schedule for residential refuse pick-up will remain unchanged.

The Kauaʻi Bus will be operating on its current daily schedule. 

Regular business hours for county offices and services will resume on Friday, Nov. 27.

For more information on recreation services, please visit the Department of Parks and Recreation website, www.kauai.gov/Parks , or call 808-241-4460.

For more information about The Kauaʻi Bus, please visit the Transportation website, www.kauai.gov/transportation , or call 808-246-8110.

For more information about recycling and waste disposal, please visit the Recycling website, www.kauai.gov/recycling , or call 808-241-4841. Please see www.kauai.gov/HI5  for location information for HI5 recycling.

headline.title: Mayor Kawakami signs Bill 2998, bringing wildfire safety standards to new homes islandwide
headline.subject: NR 11-16-26 (Mayor Kawakami signs Bill 2998, bringing wildfire safety standards to new homes islandwide)

items.body:
Mayor Kawakami signs Bill 2998, bringing wildfire safety standards to new homes islandwide

LĪHUʻE – On Monday, Nov. 16, Mayor Derek S.K. Kawakami signed into law Bill No. 2998, Draft 3, an ordinance passed by the Kauaʻi County Council on Oct. 28 that sets islandwide wildfire safety standards for new homes.

The ordinance establishes Wildfire and Wildland Urban Interface (WUI) construction requirements for new homes and substantial improvements, along with defensible space, setback, and access standards for larger new developments. It builds on Bill No. 2961, signed in September 2025, which made Kauaʻi the first county in Hawaiʻi to tie wildfire safety into zoning and permitting for West Kauaʻi’s plantation camp districts.

“Mahalo to the Kauaʻi County Council, our Planning Department, the Kauaʻi Fire Department, the Kauaʻi Emergency Management Agency, the Hawaiʻi Wildfire Management Organization, and the builders, designers, and residents who testified and helped shape this ordinance,” said Mayor Kawakami. “Lahaina taught all of Hawaiʻi that in a wind-driven fire, homes are lost to embers. We have a kuleana to learn from that before we face a disaster of our own. The homes we build today will be home to our keiki and kūpuna for generations, and this ordinance makes sure they are built with that lesson in mind.”

According to U.S. Department of Agriculture Forest Service data cited in the ordinance, homes in Kauaʻi County face a higher wildfire risk than about 91 percent of U.S. counties. The Lahaina Fire Incident Analysis Report also recommended WUI codes, ember-resistant construction, and defensible space requirements as key steps for wildfire safety statewide.

“As our climate changes, we have to do everything we can on the planning side before a fire ever starts,” said Council Planning Committee Chair Addison Bulosan. “No one takes added building costs lightly, and this Council spent months working through those questions with our community. In the end, protecting lives and homes is worth it.”

Under the ordinance, new homes will include home hardening standards, a non-combustible zone, and setback standards for future subdivisions.

“This ordinance was built for Kauaʻi, not copied from a mainland code,” said Planning Director Kaʻāina Hull. “Every requirement was weighed for its safety benefit, its cost, and whether it lets us keep building the housing our community needs. The focus is on embers and the fuels around a home, which is where homes are saved or lost.”

The cost of construction under the code will also be offset by a Kauai Water Department facilities reserve charge (FRC) waiver of $14,000 for the implementation of wildfire regulations, making many proposed homes actually cheaper to construct under the WUI bill than under current code standards.

“Most homes lost in wildfires are ignited by embers, often well ahead of the fire itself,” said Kauaʻi Fire Department Chief Michael Gibson. “A clear 5-foot zone, covered metal gutters, ember-resistant vents, and well-kept defensible space give a home a fighting chance during Red Flag Warning conditions, and they give our firefighters a safer place to work.”

The bill also addresses the rising cost of homeowners insurance. Increasing risks associated with climate-related hazards, including wildfires, are contributing to reduced insurance availability, and increasing premiums are affecting the overall affordability of home ownership. This bill aligns with wildfire mitigation standards of the Insurance Institute for Business and Home Safety (IBHS) to strengthen property resilience and help improve insurance affordability on Kauaʻi.

The Planning Department developed the ordinance over two years with the Kauaʻi Fire Department, the Kauaʻi Emergency Management Agency, the Building Division, the Hawaiʻi Wildfire Management Organization (HWMO), DoKi Wildfire Solutions, and UL Research Institutes’ Fire Safety Research Institute (FSRI).
